title: Decoder observability & graceful fallback playbook for constrained outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a reproducible, operational playbook and test harness that verifies constrained-decoder behavior under realistic streaming + tool-calling traffic patterns and provides clear observability signals plus automated graceful fallbacks. This ticket covers telemetry spec, synthetic test scenarios, canary metrics, and a small library of fallback policies (retry with compatible schema, strip tool call noise, and degrade to permissive parse).
background: We observed intermittent decoder failures when streaming JSON-mode responses while interleaving tool calls (see ops/incident summary linked below). Current mitigations are ad-hoc: retries, client-side heuristics, and model rollbacks. We need an engineering-led playbook that codifies detection, triage, and automated fallback so customer workloads stay online without manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: events emitted for partial-parse, buffer-overflow, and toolcall-interference with stable schema identifiers
Synthetic harness: 12 replay scenarios covering short/long sequences, random token drops, and mid-stream toolcall insertion; each scenario has expected outcome and pass/fail metrics

Fallbacks: implement three fallback policies with opt-in configuration: (1) strict-retry-with-delay, (2) compatible-schema-fallback (map to a relaxed schema variant), (3) permissive-parser-degrade; all reachable via API config
Canary: rollout job that runs against 1% of traffic and raises alerts on >0.5% regression in successful-parse rate within 15 minutes
Docs & Runbook: step-by-step incident runbook and onboarding doc for SRE and Solutions teams with links to dashboards and debug commands
technical_notes: Instrument events at decoder ingress/egress with correlation IDs for request, model-variant, and route
Emit sampling traces for streaming sessions longer than 2s to capture partial-stream failures
Expose parser-state metric (e.g., brackets_balance, expected_fields_remaining) as integer gauges
Design fallback toggles as per-route config in routing layer so Dedicated/private customers can pin behavior
When invoking compatible-schema-fallback, attempt deterministic transformation rather than retraining (field renames, defaulting missing arrays, wrap scalars into arrays)
Consider cost trade-offs: aggressive retries increase token spend; prefer relaxed-parse fallback for user-facing low-latency slices
test_plan: Unit: parser-state simulator with deterministic token-injection to assert state transitions
Integration: streaming harness that replays real production traces (anonymized) and injects toolcall frames at configured offsets
Chaos: fault-injection job that drops chunks and flips token orders to validate recovery behavior
E2E: canary experiments against staging model-variants with traffic shadowing and metric comparison to baseline
observability: Logs: structured logs with fields: request_id, session_id, model, seq_len, fallback_policy, failure_reason
Alerts: page when parse_failure_rate > 0.5% on production for 10m for high-SLA customers
Dashboards: per-route parse health, fallback effectiveness (success after fallback), and token-cost delta post-fallback
runbook_steps: 1) Identify affected requests via parse_failure_count and correlate request_ids to session traces
2) Check model-variant and last successful parse timestamp to determine rollback window
3) If failures spike across variants: enable compatible-schema-fallback globally and notify customers
4) If failures are isolated to a route: flip per-route fallback to permissive-parser for 5m and monitor
5) For persistent failures: run trace-level reassembly (use tools/stream-replayer) and open a model-oncall ticket with annotated example traces

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive fallbacks may mask model regressions and delay root-cause detection — Mitigation: label fallbacked requests in analytics and surface regression alerts separate from fallback metrics
Risk: cost impact from retries and longer sessions — Mitigation: default fallback order prefers low-cost transformations before token-heavy retries
Risk: compatibility mapping can introduce semantic drift for customer schemas — Mitigation: require opt-in for Reserved/Dedicated customers and provide explicit transformation logs
